headline: Highest income in Chicago pairs with the highest rent and the least sunlight in Ward 42.
summary:
Ward 42 covers the Loop, the Near North Side, West Town, and part of the Near West Side, the downtown core and the blocks immediately around it. It holds down fifth place out of the city's fifty wards. Its strengths cluster around downtown living. More residents here commute on foot or by bike than anywhere else in the city, and the ward has more mapped arts and culture spots than anywhere else in Chicago. Average income reported on tax returns filed from the ward is the highest in Chicago, and city crews close out 311 requests here faster than anywhere else, both for potholes and for rodent complaints.

The weak points line up with density and shadow. Downtown's tall buildings block a lot of direct sunlight at street level, and the ward finishes last in the city for ground-level sun access on both solstices. Pedestrian and cyclist crash counts and median rent both come in last too, and licensed child care per resident is lower here than anywhere else in Chicago. Ward 42 combines the city's top income and arts numbers with its highest rent and dimmest streets.
reading_the_rankings: Start with average income, the ward's headline number. It comes from IRS tax data apportioned across ZIP code boundaries that never lined up with ward lines to begin with, so what lands on Ward 42 really describes the ZIP codes touching it more than the ward itself. The people who publish that figure grade it low confidence, and a chunk of the fifty wards are missing the number entirely. The rent number carries a smaller version of the same problem. It gets divided among wards using each census tract's land area as a proxy for where renters actually live, so a tract that crosses into a cheaper neighboring ward can pull Ward 42's number in either direction. The child care rank has a different catch. It sits on a ward boundary recorded at the time the source counted it, and Chicago redrew those boundaries in 2023, so part of what this number reflects belongs to a ward shape that no longer exists on the map.

news.headline: Trump Tower On Obama Way? Chicago Considers Honorary Designation For Downtown Street
news.note: The ward's alderman proposed an honorary street sign for the stretch of Wabash Avenue that includes the block with Trump Tower, naming it after Barack Obama.

alderperson.name: Brendan Reilly
alderperson.verification_note: The data's website_url field was empty. Found ward42chicago.com and fetched both its homepage and its About page directly this session. The homepage reads 'Alderman Reilly represents downtown's 42nd Ward, Chicago's Central Business District and home to 90,000 residents and over 10,000 business licenses,' and the About page reads 'Alderman Brendan Reilly has served as a member of the Chicago City Council since 2007 when he unseated a 36-year incumbent,' confirming the site is his.
